<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913746_theRebbe_550" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913746_theRebbe_550__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Tzemach Tzedek explains that the superiority of the great shofar is understood through levels of pleasure, with the shofar of the Temple on Shabbat drawing from a higher pleasure than Shabbat itself, and the shofar of the First Temple being higher than that of the Second, yet even the Jubilee shofar is called a plain shofar, indicating the great shofar is above all.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And in order to explain the superiority of the great shofar even more,</t>
    <t s="2">the Tzemach Tzedek brings</t>
    <t s="3">(in his explanation</t>
    <t s="4">to the maamar beginning "And it shall be on that day, a great shofar shall be blown" in Likkutei Torah)</t>
    <t s="5">what is stated in Likkutei Torah in the maamar beginning "To understand the Mishnah"</t>
    <t s="6">"The festival of Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat, in the Temple they would blow [the shofar], but not in the provinces,"</t>
    <t s="7">that this [matter] that on Rosh HaShanah one must blow the shofar is in order to thereby arouse above the pleasure in the creation of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="8">and since on Shabbat, from its own essence, there is [already] the pleasure,</t>
    <t s="9">therefore on Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat there is no need</t>
    <t s="10">[so much]</t>
    <t s="11">for the blowing of the shofar.</t>
    <t s="12">And that in the Temple they would blow [the shofar] even on Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat is [because]</t>
    <t s="13">there are several levels in pleasure,</t>
    <t s="14">and the level of pleasure that is drawn down through the blowing of the shofar in the Temple is more elevated than the level of pleasure of Shabbat.</t>
    <t s="15">For the pleasure of Shabbat is from the aspect of the externality of Keter,</t>
    <t s="16">the root of the emanated beings,</t>
    <t s="17">and the pleasure that they drew down through the blowing of the shofar in the Temple is from the aspect of the internality of Keter,</t>
    <t s="18">the lower level within the Emanator.</t>
    <t s="19">And the Tzemach Tzedek adds,</t>
    <t s="20">that also within the pleasure of the lower level within the Emanator,</t>
    <t s="21">there are several levels.</t>
    <t s="22">And the pleasure that was drawn in the First Temple through the blowing of the shofar is more elevated than the pleasure that was drawn in the Second Temple.</t>
    <t s="23">And within the First Temple itself,</t>
    <t s="24">the shofar of Yom Kippur of the Jubilee year</t>
    <t s="25">[for the commandment of Jubilee was only in the First Temple]</t>
    <t s="26">is more elevated than the shofar of Rosh HaShanah.</t>
    <t s="27">And nevertheless, even regarding the shofar of Jubilee it is stated,</t>
    <t s="28">"And you shall sound the shofar of teruah,"</t>
    <t s="29">a plain shofar.</t>
    <t s="30">From this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="31">that the great shofar is above even the revelation that is drawn through the shofar of Jubilee.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The great shofar of the future is also above the shofar of the Giving of the Torah, which was a plain shofar, because at Sinai the people were already close to G-d, whereas to awaken the lost and scattered requires a great shofar that will blow of itself.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And to add,</t>
    <t s="2">that the great shofar that will be in the future is more elevated even than the shofar of the Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="3">for even regarding the shofar of the Giving of the Torah it is stated,</t>
    <t s="4">"And the sound of the shofar was,"</t>
    <t s="5">a plain shofar.</t>
    <t s="6">For that which the verse continues, "the sound of the shofar grew exceedingly strong" is that the sound of the shofar was very strong,</t>
    <t s="7">a great sound,</t>
    <t s="8">but regarding the shofar itself from which the sound emanated,</t>
    <t s="9">it is not stated that it was a great shofar,</t>
    <t s="10">and from this it is understood that the great shofar that will be in the future is above even the shofar of the Giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="11">And as it is brought in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer</t>
    <t s="12">regarding the two horns of the ram of Yitzchak,</t>
    <t s="13">that the left horn, its sound was heard at Mount Sinai, as it is stated, "And the sound of the shofar was,"</t>
    <t s="14">and the right horn, which is greater than the left, is destined to be blown with it in the future,</t>
    <t s="15">as it is stated, "And it shall be on that day, a great shofar shall be blown."</t>
    <t s="16">And the reason for this, that the shofar of the Giving of the Torah was a plain shofar and the shofar of the future will be a great shofar,</t>
    <t s="17">the Mitteler Rebbe explains,</t>
    <t s="18">for at the Giving of the Torah they were all in closeness to G-dliness</t>
    <t s="19">(even before the sound of the shofar),</t>
    <t s="20">and therefore even through a plain shofar it was possible to awaken them.</t>
    <t s="21">But in order to awaken the lost and the scattered, it is specifically through a great shofar.</t>
    <t s="22">And based on this, he explains what is written, "a great shofar shall be blown,"</t>
    <t s="23">that the word "yitaka" (shall be blown)</t>
    <t s="24">(with a kamatz under the tav)</t>
    <t s="25">indicates that it will blow of itself,</t>
    <t s="26">for the revelation of the aspect of the great shofar to awaken the lost and the scattered will be of itself,</t>
    <t s="27">without any arousal from below at all.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The maamar explains that on Rosh HaShanah, the drawing down of will and pleasure is now through man's service, which is superior to the initial creation, yet the current shofar is a plain shofar drawn by human effort, while the future great shofar will be drawn of itself without any arousal from below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, it is explained at the beginning of the maamar</t>
    <t s="2">(after the precise analysis of the verse "And it shall be on that day, a great shofar shall be blown")</t>
    <t s="3">that which we say,</t>
    <t s="4">"On Rosh HaShanah, 'This day is the beginning of Your works,'" for on every Rosh HaShanah there is a renewal of all the worlds, just as it was the first time.</t>
    <t s="5">And what is stated, "A remembrance of the first day"</t>
    <t s="6">(that Rosh HaShanah is only a remembrance of the first day)</t>
    <t s="7">is [explained as follows]:</t>
    <t s="8">for at the beginning of creation,</t>
    <t s="9">the drawing down of the will and pleasure in the creation of the worlds was from His own essence,</t>
    <t s="10">for "He desires kindness,"</t>
    <t s="11">and now, the matter depends on an arousal from below.</t>
    <t s="12">And he explains</t>
    <t s="13">that the service</t>
    <t s="14">(the arousal from below)</t>
    <t s="15">through which the will and pleasure in the creation of the worlds are drawn down is as per the statement of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="16">"Recite before Me [verses of] Kingship... Remembrances... and with what? With the shofar."</t>
    <t s="17">And the reason for this, that the drawing down now is through the service of man, is</t>
    <t s="18">because through the fact that the drawing down</t>
    <t s="19">(now)</t>
    <t s="20">is through the service of Israel,</t>
    <t s="21">for the root of Israel is in the Awtsmoos,</t>
    <t s="22">the will and pleasure that are drawn down now are more elevated than the will and pleasure that were drawn from His own essence</t>
    <t s="23">(at the beginning of creation).</t>
    <t s="24">And based on this, it must be understood,</t>
    <t s="25">that the shofar from above</t>
    <t s="26">(the innerness of the supernal will)</t>
    <t s="27">that is drawn down now,</t>
    <t s="28">which is a plain shofar,</t>
    <t s="29">its drawing down is through the service of man,</t>
    <t s="30">and the shofar of the future, which is a great shofar,</t>
    <t s="31">will be drawn of itself, without any arousal from below at all.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
